BURHAN:v1p490/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p490/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p490/r3.claim: He asks why some examples compare things without naming the subjects, unlike the explicit contrasts in 35:19–22.
BURHAN:v1p490/r3.anchor: فإن قلت فى بعض هذه الأمثلة تشبيه أشياء بأشياء لم يذكر فيها المشبهات وهلا صرح بها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p25/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p25/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p25/r5.claim: The majority read الأحياء with masculine agreement, while Zādān from al-Kisāʾī has feminine agreement; the order is eloquent because it moves from believer/unbeliever to their light and final dwelling.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p25/r5.anchor: وقرأ زادان عن الكسائي: وما تستوي الأحياء، بتاء التأنيث والجمهور: بالياء،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p26/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p26/r1.speaker: الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p26/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī says the living/dead contrast is stronger than blind/seeing: the blind may share some perception with the seeing, whereas the spiritually dead cannot receive truth usefully.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p26/r1.anchor: إذ الأعمى قد يشارك البصير في إدراك ما، والكافر غير مدرك إدراكا نافعا، فهو كالميت،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p26/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p26/r4.speaker: الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p26/r4.claim: For al-Rāzī, the living are believers who accepted revelation and the dead are those who heard clear signs but gained no benefit; he sees them as later than the believers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p26/r4.anchor: وما يستوي الأحياء: الذين آمنوا بما أنزل الله، ولا الأموات: الذين تليت عليهم الآيات البينات،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p27/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p27/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p27/r1.claim: God's causing people to hear means granting the response that leads to faith; the resistant audience is like the dead in graves because their hearts are dead to truth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p27/r1.anchor: وكنى بالإسماع عن الذي تكون عنه الإجابة للإيمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p27/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p27/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p27/r2.claim: Al-Ashhab and al-Ḥasan read بمسمع من as an annexation; the majority retain tanwīn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p27/r2.anchor: وقرأ الأشهب، والحسن بمسمع من، على الإضافة والجمهور: بالتنوين.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p27/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p27/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p27/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān summarizes al-Rāzī's argument that the living/dead contrast is strongest: no dead person matches a living person's perception.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p27/r7.anchor: من كلام أبي عبد الله الرازي، وفيه بعض تلخيص.

STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r7.claim: The discussion of Satan as Deluder and enemy leads into a contrast between believers and disbelievers, including a poetic contrast in verses 19–22.
STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r7.anchor: A discussion of Satan as the Deluder and enemy (vv. 5–8) leads into the other major theme of this sūrah, the contrast between the believers and the disbelievers

STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r8.claim: Verses 19–22 offer one of the Quran’s most poetic contrasts between believers and disbelievers.
STUDYQURAN:35:intro/r8.anchor: vv. 19–22 provide one of the most poetic contrasts between the two groups

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p263/r8.claim: The passage refutes polytheism and intercession and tells the Prophet to leave stubborn idolaters' fate to God after fulfilling his duty.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p297/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p297/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p297/r1.claim: Al-ʿAzīz denotes God's invincible dominance and al-Ḥakīm His wise action; their perfect realization leaves no room for partners.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p297/r1.anchor: the attribute ُزیِزَعْال shows that He is inaccessible, dominant and powerful; the attribute ُمیِكَحْال implies that all actions of God are based on great wisdom.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p297/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p297/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p297/r2.claim: A partner needed to create or govern would negate God's might, while one who could sway His justice would negate His wisdom; these are the idolaters' two misconceptions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p297/r2.anchor: both these misconceptions were the real cause of the polytheism of the Idolaters.

SAMIN-DURR:35:22/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:22/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:35:22/r1.claim: The contrasts symbolize disbeliever and believer, disbelief and faith, falsehood and truth, and those who enter Islam versus those outside; their order follows the paired images and verse endings.
SAMIN-DURR:35:22/r1.anchor: وهذه الأشياء جيء بها على سبيل الاستعارة والتمثيل، فالأعمى والبصير، الكافر والمؤمن، والظلمات والنور، الكفر والإيمان،

SAMIN-DURR:35:22/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:22/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:35:22/r3.claim: Repeating the verb intensifies the contrast of living and dead, stronger than the earlier pairs because they share fewer faculties.
SAMIN-DURR:35:22/r3.anchor: وإنما كرر الفعل في قوله: { وما يستوي الأحيآء } مبالغة في ذلك؛ لأن المنافاة بين الحياة والموت أتم

SAMIN-DURR:35:22/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:22/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:35:22/r4.claim: لا is not repeated for blind and sighted because a person can pass between those states; the other pairs permanently exclude one another, while life and death differ most completely.
SAMIN-DURR:35:22/r4.anchor: ولم يعد " لا " تأكيدا في قوله: " الأعمى والبصير " وكررها في غيره؛ لأن منافاة ما بعده أتم

SAMIN-DURR:35:19-22/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:19-22/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:35:19-22/r3.claim: Both living and dead are plural because their difference is greatest: no dead person equals a living person in perception, comparing kinds or individuals.
SAMIN-DURR:35:19-22/r3.anchor: وإنما جمع الأحياء والأموات لأن التفاوت بينهما أكثر؛ إذ ما من ميت يساوي في الإدراك حيا

ASAD-NOTES:35:19/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:35:19/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:35:19/r1.claim: Asad glosses the living and dead as spiritually alive or dead, extending the metaphor to those described as lying in graves.
ASAD-NOTES:35:19/r1.anchor: the living and the dead [of heart]

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p346/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p346/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p346/r1.claim: Against the passage's background, the righteous realize and refine their capacities while the truth is conclusively delivered to wrongdoers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p346/r1.anchor: potentials of the righteous materialize and are polished and the truth is conclusively delivered to the wrong-doers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p348/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p348/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p348/r1.claim: The Prophet worried that his people's indifference reflected a shortcoming in him; God reassures him that he must address the living, while the spiritually and intellectually dead will not respond however much he wishes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p348/r1.anchor: To dispel this worry, the Almighty has assured him through various styles in this verse. He is told that his duty is to make the living listen to his message and not the dead.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p348/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p348/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p348/r2.claim: Here 'making hear' means urging and propelling someone to hear and accept.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p348/r2.anchor: the word سماعإِ means to urge and propel someone to hear and accept something.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p348/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p348/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p348/r3.claim: God grants the urge to listen and understand according to His wisdom: people who preserve their natural abilities receive it, while those who neglect them become morally and spiritually dead and can be revived only by God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p348/r3.anchor: those who keep alive the natural abilities bestowed to them by Him find in themselves the divinely given urge to listen and understand further.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r1.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r1.claim: Al-Ṭībī takes the living and dead as anaphoric references to believers who accepted the message after the mission and disbelievers who persisted arrogantly.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r1.anchor: تمثيل آخر للمؤمنين الذين دخلوا في الدين بعد البعثة والكافرين الذين أصروا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r2.claim: Another view takes the living and dead to mean scholars and the ignorant.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r2.anchor: فالتعريف كما قال الطيبي للعهد وقيل : للعلماء والجهلاء

ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r3.speaker: الثعالبي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r3.claim: Al-Thaʿālibī makes the blind and sighted, rather than the living and dead, the two figures for believers and disbelievers; al-Ālūsī rejects this.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r3.anchor: والثعالبي جعل الأعمى والبصير مثلين لهما وليس بذاك

ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r4.claim: God makes whom He wills hear and enables them to perceive sounds.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r5.speaker: الخفاجي وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r5.claim: Al-Khafājī and others suggest the hearing is attentive acceptance and reflection on God’s signs.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r5.anchor: وقال الخفاجي وغيره : ولعل في الآية ما يقتضي

ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r6.claim: The grave image extends the comparison of the obstinate disbelievers with the dead and despairs the Prophet of their conversion; the emphatic bāʾ is extra.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r6.anchor: ترشيح لتمثيل المصرين على الكفر بالأموات وأشباع في إقناطه عليه الصلاة والسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r7.claim: The negated hearing is ordinary, effective hearing, not an absolute denial that the dead can hear; the report about the well victims describes an extraordinary event, like God’s attribution of the Prophet’s throwing to Himself.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r7.anchor: والمراد بالسماع هنا ما أريد به في سابقه ولا يأبى إرادة السماع المعروف ماورد في حديث القليب

ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r8.claim: The analogies progress from the two seas (35:12) to blind and sighted with darkness, light, shade, and heat, then to living and dead, intensifying the contrast and adding the loss of external light before reaching death.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r8.anchor: وما ألطف نظم هذه التمثيلات فقد شبه المؤمن والكافر أولا بالبحرين وفضل البحر الأجاج

ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r9.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r9.claim: Al-Ṭībī says omission of the emphatic لا in the blind/sighted comparison prepares for the next living/dead comparison and explains its repeated opening; later pairs have لا because they stand as independent figures for truth, falsehood, reward, and punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r9.anchor: ذكر الطيبي أن إخلاء الثاني من لا المؤكدة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r10.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r10.claim: The inserted لا does not mean different kinds of darkness fail to equal one another; the intended contrasts are darkness with light, shade with heat, and living with dead.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186#5/r10.anchor: أن الظلمات لا تساوي النور والظل لا يساوي الحرور

ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says each لا implies repetition before the paired noun, with the initial terms standing for the omitted second terms; al-Ālūsī says treating لا as emphatic makes this deletion unnecessary.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r1.anchor: وزعم إبن عطية أن دخول لا على نية التكرار

ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r3.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r3.claim: The Imām says life and death are more completely opposed than sight and blindness: sighted and blind may share perception, while the dead differs from the living in its very reality.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r3.anchor: وإن كانا كالأعمى والبصير من حيث أن الجسم الواحد قد يكون حيا ثم يعرض له الموت

ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r4.claim: One explanation says لا is omitted from the first pair because the listener readily understands the intended contrast, then repeated afterward.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r4.anchor: وقيل لم تكر قيل وكررت بعد لأن المخاطب في أول الكلام لا يقصر في فهم المراد

ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r5.claim: Another explanation says later لا prevents reading the phrase as denying equality between the combined groups, and the last repetition marks special emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r5.anchor: وقيل كررت فيما عدا الأخير لأنه لو قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r8.claim: The living precede the dead because they represent believers after the message and the dead represent those persisting in disbelief; the next clause about whom God makes hear supports this.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r8.anchor: وقدم الأحياء على الأموات ولم يعكس الأمر ليوافق الأولين في تقديم غير الأشرف

ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r9.claim: Another explanation says earlier pairs put nonexistence first, but here death follows life because the intended dead are those who first had life, as the grave image confirms.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r9.anchor: وقيل قدم ما قدم فيما عدا الأخير لأنه عدم وله مرتبة السبق

ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r10.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187/r10.claim: A further explanation says placing the less noble first does not diminish the superior one’s rank, even though the order signals their difference.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p187#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187#2/r1.claim: Fire can be surmounted by smoke and horsemen’s turbans by dust, illustrating how what seems subordinate may be placed above what is more noble.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187#2/r1.anchor: فالنار يعلوها الدخان وربما يعلو الغبار عمائم الفرسان

ALUSI-FULL:v22p187#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187#2/r4.claim: Living and dead are plural because there are multiple referents; blind and sighted remain singular to express a generic class and preserve cadence.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187#2/r4.anchor: وجمع الأحياء والأموات على بابه لتعدد المشبه بهما ولم يجمع الأعمى والبصير

ALUSI-FULL:v22p187#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187#2/r5.speaker: الأشهب والحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v22p187#2/r5.claim: Al-Ashhab and al-Ḥasan read بمسمع من with an iḍāfa construction.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#3/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#3/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#3/r7.claim: The living and dead mean believers and unbelievers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#3/r7.anchor: {وما يستوي الأحياء ولا الأموات} يعني: المؤمنين والكفار.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#3/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#3/r8.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#3/r8.claim: Another view takes them to mean scholars and the ignorant.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#3/r8.anchor: يعني: المؤمنين والكفار. وقيل: العلماء والجهال.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#4/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#4/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#4/r1.claim: God makes whomever He wills hear so that they heed and respond.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#4/r1.anchor: {إن الله يسمع من يشاء} حتى يتعظ ويجيب،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#4/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#4/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#4/r2.claim: Those in graves are unbelievers, likened to the dead because they do not respond.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#4/r2.anchor: {وما أنت بمسمع من في القبور} يعني: الكفار، شبههم بالأموات في القبور حين لم يجيبوا.

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:19-22/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:19-22/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:19-22/r7.claim: Living and dead again represent believers and unbelievers, a stronger comparison hence repeated verb; alternatively, scholars and ignorant people.
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:19-22/r7.anchor: تمثيل آخر للمؤمنين والكافرين أبلغ من الأول

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:19-22/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:19-22/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:19-22/r8.claim: God enables whomever He wills to understand His signs and take admonition.
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:19-22/r8.anchor: هدايته فيوفقه لفهم آياته والاتعاظ بعظاته.

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:19-22/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:19-22/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:19-22/r9.claim: Calling persistent unbelievers dead extends the metaphor and tells the Prophet to give up hope of making them hear.
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:19-22/r9.anchor: ترشيح لتمثيل المصرين على الكفر بالأموات ومبالغة في إقناطه عنهم.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r5.claim: Life comes first because it is what manifests the differences under discussion.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r6.claim: The verse repeats the verb, going beyond the blind-and-seeing example because blind people still share some perceptions; believers receive two analogies with different rhetorical functions.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r6.anchor: الأعمى يشارك البصير في بعض الإدراكات

BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r7.claim: Living people differ in speech, intelligence, temperament, and ease of manner; scarcely any two are alike in every trait.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r8.claim: The dead represent unbelievers and vary in the difficulty of death and decay, as well as in the hidden misery or felicity that unbelievers refuse to acknowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r8.anchor: أي الذين هم مثال للكافرين في صعوبة الموت وسهولته والبلى وغيره مما يخفى ولا يقر به الكفار من الشقاوة والسعادة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r9.claim: These examples clearly show God’s free agency and the error of associating partners with Him, since nothing resembles Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r9.anchor: من وضوح الدلالة على الفعل بالاختيار وعلى ضلال من أشرك به شيئا لأنه لا يشابهه شيء

BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r10.claim: God gives hearing, meaning guidance, to whom He wills and deafens, blinds, overturns, or ruins whom He wills among living hearts and spirits and dead meanings and forms.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r10.anchor: أي فيهديه ولو لم يكن له قابلية في العادة كالجمادات

BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r11.claim: If response to revelation depended on natural capacity, everyone would accept or reject alike, since the call and displayed miracles reach them on equal terms.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r11.anchor: لأن نسبة الدعوة وإظهار المعجزة إليهم على حد سواء

BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r12.claim: God’s selective granting of receptive hearing explains why warning benefits those He wills, confirming the earlier statement that only those who fear God gain from it and consoling the Prophet.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r12.anchor: وإن الإنذار إنما هو لمن قضى بانتفاعه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p218/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p218/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p218/r1.claim: Those who turn away are like the dead because they gain no benefit from the extraordinary signs they see and hear.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p218/r1.anchor: ولما كان المعرض قد ساوى الميت في حاله التي هي عدم الانتفاع بما يرى ويسمع من الخوارق

BIQAI-FULL:v6p218/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p218/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p218/r2.claim: The nominal expression stresses that the Prophet has no power to make them hear by himself, apart from God's enabling him.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p218/r2.anchor: معبرًا بالأسمية تنبيها على عدم إثبات ذلك له صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p218/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p218/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p218/r3.claim: The graves are physical and metaphorical; only God can grant hearing that benefits them, if He wills, so the Prophet need not grieve over them.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p218/r3.anchor: بل الله يسمعهم إن شاء فلا تذهب نفسك عليهم حسرات

BIQAI-FULL:v6p218/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p218/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p218/r4.claim: The verse is evidence for resurrection.

DURR-FULL:v7p17/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r6.claim: The believer is alive in influence, sight, intention, and deeds; the disbeliever is dead in each of these.
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r6.anchor: وفي قوله {وما يستوي} قال: خلق فضل بعضه على بعض فأما المؤمن فعبد حي الأثر حي البصر

DURR-FULL:v7p17/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r8.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r8.claim: Al-Suddī identifies shade as Paradise, scorching heat as Hell, and the living and dead as believer and disbeliever.
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r8.anchor: السدي رضي الله عنه في قوله {وما يستوي الأعمى والبصير} قال: الكافر والمؤمن

DURR-FULL:v7p17/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r9.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r9.claim: God makes hear whom He wills means that He guides whom He wills.
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r9.anchor: {إن الله يسمع من يشاء} قال: يهدي من يشاء

DURR-FULL:v7p17/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that after Badr the Prophet addressed named slain enemies; when asked if they heard, he said they heard no better than the living did, and the verse was revealed as a likeness for disbelievers.
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله (فإنك لا تسمع الموتى) (الروم 52) {وما أنت بمسمع من في القبور}

DURR-FULL:v7p18/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p18/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p18/r1.claim: Just as those in graves cannot be made to hear, a disbeliever neither hears nor benefits from what he hears.
DURR-FULL:v7p18/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {وما أنت بمسمع من في القبور} فكذلك الكافر لا يسمع ولا ينتفع بما يسمع

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3179#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3179#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3179#3/r1.claim: Qatada says the unbeliever, like someone in a grave, neither hears nor benefits from what he hears. He adds that every community had a messenger from God, and that earlier messengers brought proofs, scriptures, and a clear Book; God swiftly punished their deniers in this world and then consigned them to the Fire.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3179#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : وما انت بمسمع من في القبور فكذلك الكافر لا يسمع ولا يتنفع بما يسمع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p291/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p291/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p291/r4.claim: Verses 19–23 distribute four sensory analogies across people, belief, and its effects: unbeliever/blind, disbelief/darkness and heat, believer/seeing, faith/light and shade, and believers as living versus the dead.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p291/r4.anchor: أربعة أمثال للمؤمنين والكافرين ، وللإيمان والكفر ، شبه الكافر بالأعمى ، والكفر بالظلمات ، والحرور والكافر بالميت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p291/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p291/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p291/r5.claim: The disbeliever and disbelief are described first to stress their repellent condition; the analogies clarify the relative restriction on effective warning in 35:18.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p291/r5.anchor: وقدم تشبيه حال الكافر وكفره على تشبيه حال المؤمن وإيمانه ابتداء لأن الغرض الأهم من هذا التشبيه هو تفظيع حال الكافر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p292/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p292/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p292/r8.claim: The two conjunctions introducing darkness and shade connect clauses and organize three comparisons, one spanning both groups; the implied clauses are that darkness and shade do not equal their counterparts, made explicit in the final comparison.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p292/r8.anchor: عاطف جملة على جملة وعاطف تشبيهات ثلاثة بل تشبيه منها يجمع الفريقين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p294/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p294/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p294/r3.claim: The explicit verb يستوي in the living-and-dead clause supplies the verb omitted from the two preceding clauses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p294/r3.anchor: أظهر في هذه الجملة الفعل الذي قدر في الجملتين اللتين قبلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p294/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p294/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p294/r4.claim: The comparison returns to believers and disbelievers and escalates from believer as sighted and disbeliever as blind to believer as living and disbeliever as dead; a parallel sequence occurs in al-Raʿd.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p294/r4.anchor: فهذا ارتقاء في تشبيه الحالين من تشبيه المؤمن بالبصير والكافر بالأعمى إلى تشبيه المؤمن بالحي والكافر بالميت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p294/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p294/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p294/r5.claim: Life enables perception and action, while death stops them; faith brings good and receptivity to understanding like a new life, whereas kufr cuts off beneficial action and reception of guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p294/r5.anchor: لما كانت الحياة هي مبعث المدارك والمساعي كلها وكان الموت قاطعا للمدارك والمساعي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p294/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p294/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p294/r6.claim: The text alternates comparisons of persons with comparisons of faith and kufr because the paired states entail one another; the personal comparisons are clearer in two places and the reverse framing clearer in the other two.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p294/r6.anchor: واكتفي بتشبيه الكافر والمؤمن في موضعين عن تشبيه الكفر والإيمان وبالعكس لتلازمهما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295/r1.claim: The clearest way kufr resembles death is that disbelievers do not benefit from the Quran, while believers receive, study, and understand it; the cited verses contrast rejecting its recitation with following the best guidance heard.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295/r1.anchor: لما كان أعظم حرمان نشأ عن الكفر هو حرمان الانتفاع بأبلغ كلام وأصدقه وهو القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295/r2.claim: After the living-and-dead simile, addressing the Prophet excuses his duty to preach to both groups and consoles him: acceptance depends on God preparing a heart, while rejection reflects a dead heart; the hearing phrase answers the earlier comparison in matching order.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295/r2.anchor: وأعقب تمثيل حال المؤمنين والكافرين بحال الأحياء والأموات بتوجيه الخطاب إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295/r3.claim: God’s making some hear explains the restriction that only those who fear their Lord unseen are warned: the restriction implies one group benefits and another does not.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295/r3.anchor: تعليل لجملة { إنما تنذر الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295#2/r1.claim: Those in the graves represent the people whom God has not willed to hear the Prophet’s warning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295#2/r1.anchor: إشارة إلى الذين لم يشأ الله أن يسمعهم إنذارك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295#2/r2.claim: The grave-dwellers are a metaphor for those untouched by warnings; saying they are in graves adds that earth blocks sounds, a nuance lost by simply saying the dead.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295#2/r2.anchor: لأن من في القبور أعرق في الابتعاد عن بلوغ الأصوات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295#2/r3.claim: Plural forms for living and dead vary the expression after singular blind and sighted; generic singular and plural are equivalent for class nouns with individual members, unlike light, shade, and heat.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p295#2/r3.anchor: تفننا في الكلام بعد أن أورد الأعمى والبصير بالإفراد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435#2/r1.claim: Disbelievers are likened to the blind, darkness, and dead; believers to the sighted and light, because unbelievers neither understand remembrance nor accept it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435#2/r1.anchor: مضمن هذه الآية طعن على الكفرة وتمثيل لهم بالعمى والظلمات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435#2/r6.claim: Believers are alive and unbelievers dead in that unbelievers fail to understand remembrance or attend to it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435#2/r6.anchor: وشبه المؤمنين ب الأحياء والكفرة ب الأموات من حيث لا يفهمون الذكر ولا يقبلون عليه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435#2/r7.claim: The statement returns the matter of hearing to God’s will.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435#2/r7.anchor: ثم رد الأمر إلى مشيئة الله تعالى بقوله إن الله يسمع من يشاء،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435#2/r8.claim: The verse compares unbelievers with the dead in graves, whose inability to hear is familiar to everyone.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435#2/r8.anchor: تمثيل بما يحسه البشر ويعهده جميعنا من أن الميت الذي في القبر لا يسمع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya does not place spirits in graves generally: reports put faithful spirits in trees near the Throne or in lamps, and unbelieving spirits in Sijjīn, though spirits may sometimes be near graves and hear. The dead hear footsteps or the people of Badr when their spirits are restored.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435#2/r9.anchor: وأما الأرواح فلا نقول إنها في القبر بل تتضمن الأحاديث أن أرواح المؤمنين في شجر عند العرش

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436/r1.speaker: عمر وابنه عبد الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the verse does not contradict the report about the well: God restored the dead men’s spirits to rebuke them; he prefers ʿUmar and his son ʿAbd Allāh’s position, citing the Prophet’s statement that they hear no less than the living.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436/r1.anchor: وهذا على قول عمر وابنه عبد الله وهو الصحيح إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال «ما أنتم بأسمع منهم»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436/r2.claim: ʿĀʾisha holds the Prophet did not make the dead hear but meant to reproach the living unbelievers; she used this verse as evidence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436/r2.anchor: وأما عائشة فمذهبها أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يسمعهم وأنه إنما قصد توبيخ الأحياء من الكفرة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436/r3.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan reads bi-masmiʿin with an annexation construction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن أبي الحسن «بمسمع من» على الإضافة،

BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r1.claim: The living and dead are another, stronger image for believers and unbelievers: the repeated verb and plural forms stress their contrast, and believers use life for remembrance outwardly and reflection inwardly.
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r1.anchor: تمثيل آخر للمؤمنين والكافرين أبلغ من الأول ولذلك كرر الفعل وأوثرت صيغة الجمع

BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r2.claim: Here the living is what possesses sensory power, while the dead is what has lost it; the unbeliever's outward conduct is idle and inward state false.

BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r3.speaker: بعض العلماء
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r3.claim: Some scholars take the image as scholars versus the ignorant, since likening ignorant people to the dead is familiar; a cited couplet calls the ignorant a dead person in a shroud.
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء : هو تمثيل للعلماء والجهال وتشبيه الجهلة بالأموات شائع

BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r4.claim: True life belongs to spirits and hearts through wisdom and knowledge of realities; bodily life alone has no special value because animals share it.
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r4.anchor: لأن الحياة المعتبرة هي حياة الأرواح والقلوب وذلك بالحكم والمعارف ولا عبرة بحياة الأجساد

BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r5.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r5.claim: Some Sufi masters say the truly living are those who attain real life through total annihilation, dying voluntarily before death by effacing their acts, attributes, and selves in God's.
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r5.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : الأحياء عند التحقيق هم الواصلون بالفناء التام إلى الحياة الحقيقية

BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r6.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r6.claim: The Prophet is quoted as saying that whoever wants to see a moving dead person should look at Abu Bakr, illustrating the Sufi language of voluntary death.
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r6.anchor: وإليه الإشارة بقوله عليه السلام : "من أراد أن ينظر إلى ميت متحرك فلينظر إلى أبي بكر"

BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r7.claim: Spiritual life endures, unlike bodily life, which ends with death; felicity belongs to those with lasting life and their companions and disciples.
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r7.anchor: فالحياة المعنوية لا يطرأ عليها الفناء بخلاف الحياة الصورية فإنها تزول بالموت

BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r8.speaker: أبو يزيد
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r8.claim: Ibrahim al-Harawi recounts Abu Yazid saying that ordinary people take knowledge from the dead, while his group takes divinely inspired knowledge from the Ever-Living without study or effort.
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r8.anchor: قال إبراهيم الهروي : كنت بمجلس أبي يزيد البسطامي قدس سره فقال بعضهم : إن فلانا أخذ العلم

BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r9.speaker: سعدي
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r9.claim: Saadi's lines say that people are more than bones and outward forms, and that not every form contains a living soul and meaning.
BURSEVI:v7p264#2/r9.anchor: نه مردم همين استخوانند ويوسف نه هر صورتى جان ومعنى دروست

BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r1.claim: God makes the person He wills hear with understanding and heedfulness by reviving the heart, so that the person benefits from the warning.
BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r1.anchor: كلامه إسماع فهم واتعاظ وذلك بإحياء القلب

BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r2.claim: Qabr means the place where a dead person is laid, and qabar-tu means I placed him in the grave.
BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r2.anchor: جمع قبر وهو مقر الميت وقبرته جعلته في القبر

BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r3.claim: The grave image extends the comparison: just as the buried cannot hear or answer, people sealed in unbelief cannot hear or accept truth; it further discourages the Prophet from expecting their conversion.
BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r3.anchor: وهذا الكلام ترشيح لتمثيل المصرين على الكفر بالأموات وإشباع في إقناطه عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r5.claim: Together with 28:56 and 3:128, this wording distinguishes God's station from the Prophet's so the community will not confuse them as earlier peoples did when they called Ezra or Jesus God's son.
BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r5.anchor: وقوله : {إن الله يسمع} الخ وقوله : {إنك لا تهدى من أحببت

BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r6.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r6.claim: At Badr the Prophet addressed the dead in the well, asking whether they found God's promise true; he said they heard his words no less than the living, though they could not answer.
BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r6.anchor: فقال عليه السلام : "ما أنتم بأسمع لما أقول منهم غير أنهم لا يستطيعون أن يردوا شيئا"

BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r7.claim: Bursevī reconciles the Badr report by suggesting God revived the well's dead to hear the Prophet as humiliation and regret; a dead person as such does not hear.
BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r7.anchor: قلت : أما الأول فيحتمل أن الله تعالى أحيى أهل القليب حينئذ حتى سمعوا كلام رسول الله

BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r8.claim: The saying that the dead heard no less than the living indicates that spirits hear better than bodies with souls, because the veil of sense is removed and rent.
BURSEVI:v7p264#3/r8.anchor: يدل على أن الأرواح أسمع من الأجساد مع الأرواح لزوال حجاب الحس وانخراقه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r1.speaker: قول غير مسمى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r1.claim: One interpretation takes the living as believers and the dead as unbelievers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r1.anchor: أحدهما أن الأحياء المؤمنون والأموات الكفار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r2.speaker: قول غير مسمى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r2.claim: A second interpretation takes the living as intelligent people and the dead as ignorant people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r2.anchor: والثاني أن الأحياء العقلاء والأموات الجهال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r3.speaker: قول غير مسمى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r3.claim: One grammatical view treats the lām as extra for emphasis.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r3.anchor: وفي لا المذكورة في هذه الآية قولان أحدهما أنها زائدة مؤكدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r4.speaker: قول غير مسمى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r4.claim: Another grammatical view takes lā as a negation that denies equality between the two groups.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r4.anchor: والثاني أنها نافية لاستواء أحد المذكورين مع الآخر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r5.claim: Qatāda says the comparisons are similitudes for believer and unbeliever, who are as unequal as the listed pairs.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r5.anchor: قال قتادة هذه أمثال ضربها الله تعالى للمؤمن والكافر يقول كما لا تستوي هذه الأشياء كذلك لا يستوي الكافر والمؤمن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r6.claim: God makes whomever He wills understand.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r7.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي، الحسن، الجحدري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r7.claim: Al-Sulamī, al-Ḥasan, and al-Jaḥdarī read bi-musmiʿin man with genitive annexation; the dead are a likeness for unbelievers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p483#4/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي والحسن والجحدري بمسمع من على الإضافة يعني الكفار شبههم بالموتى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542#2/r1.claim: Just as blindness and sight, darkness and light, and shade and heat differ, so do the living believers and dead disbelievers; 6:122 and 11:24 illustrate the contrast.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542#2/r1.anchor: كذلك لا تستوي الأحياء ولا الأموات، وهذا مثل ضربه الله للمؤمنين وهم الأحياء، وللكافرين وهم الأموات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542#2/r2.claim: Believers are seeing and hearing, walking in light on a straight path in both worlds, until they reach gardens of shade and springs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542#2/r2.anchor: فالمؤمن سميع بصير في نور يمشي، على صراط مستقيم في الدنيا والآخرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542#2/r3.claim: Disbelievers are blind and deaf, wandering in darkness toward scorching heat, burning wind, boiling water, and the shade of black smoke, neither cool nor gracious.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542#2/r3.anchor: حتى يفضي به ذلك إلى الحرور والسموم والحميم، {وظل من يحموم لا بارد ولا كريم} [الواقعة: 43، 44]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p543/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p543/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p543/r1.claim: God makes whomever He wills hear by guiding them to hear the proof, accept it, and submit to it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p543/r1.anchor: أي: يهديهم إلى سماع الحجة وقبولها والانقياد لها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p543/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p543/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p543/r2.claim: As the dead disbelievers do not benefit from guidance after death, the Prophet cannot make the doomed polytheists hear or guide them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p543/r2.anchor: كذلك هؤلاء المشركون الذين كتب عليهم الشقاوة لا حيلة لك فيهم، ولا تستطيع هدايتهم

MUQATIL:35:21-24/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:35:21-24/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:35:21-24/r2.claim: The living are believers and the dead are unbelievers; sight and blindness, light and darkness, and life and death picture believer and unbeliever.
MUQATIL:35:21-24/r2.anchor: المؤمنين { ولا الأموات } يعني الكفار والبصير

MUQATIL:35:21-24/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:35:21-24/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:35:21-24/r3.claim: God causes whom He wills to hear faith.
MUQATIL:35:21-24/r3.anchor: إن الله يسمع } الإيمان { من يشاء

MUQATIL:35:21-24/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:35:21-24/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:35:21-24/r4.claim: God likens living unbelievers who do not heed the call to faith to the dead in graves who cannot hear a summons.
MUQATIL:35:21-24/r4.anchor: شبه الكافر من الأحياء حين دعوا إلى الإيمان فلم يسمعوا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p341#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p341#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p341#4/r1.claim: The living symbolize those who entered Islam and the dead those who did not.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p341#4/r1.anchor: مثل الذين دخلوا فى الاسلام والذين لم يدخلوا فيه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p341#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p341#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p341#4/r2.claim: The extra la strengthens negation; the different waw connections pair some even with even and others odd with odd.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p341#4/r2.anchor: وزيادة لا لتأكيد معنى النفى والفرق بين هذه الواوات أن بعضها ضمت شفعا إلى شفع وبعضها وترا إلى وتر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p341#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p341#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p341#4/r3.claim: God knows who will enter Islam and guides whom He wills; the Prophet cannot make the dead hear, since people's fate is hidden from him and he strains over those abandoned to disbelief.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p341#4/r3.anchor: يعنى أنه قد علم من يدخل فى الإسلام ممن لا يدخل فيه فيهدى من يشاء هدايته وأما أنت فخفى عليك أمرهم فلذلك تحرص على اسلام قوم مخذولين حبه الكفار بالموتى

QURTUBI-FULL:35:19-22/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:19-22/r15.speaker: ابن قتيبة
QURTUBI-FULL:35:19-22/r15.claim: Ibn Qutayba identifies the living as rational and the dead as ignorant.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:19-22/r15.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة: الأحياء العقلاء، والأموات الجهال.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:19-22/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:19-22/r16.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:35:19-22/r16.claim: Qatada says these are comparisons: just as the pairs differ, believer and unbeliever differ.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:19-22/r16.anchor: قال قتادة: هذه كلها أمثال أي كما لا تستوي هذه الأشياء كذلك لا يستوي الكافر والمؤمن.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:19-22/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:19-22/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:19-22/r17.claim: God enables His people to hear; grave-dwellers are unbelievers whose hearts disbelief has killed.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:19-22/r17.anchor: أي يسمع أولياءه الذين خلقهم لجنته.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:19-22/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:19-22/r18.speaker: الحسن وعيسى الثقفي وعمرو بن ميمون
QURTUBI-FULL:35:19-22/r18.claim: They read without tanwin for ease; unbelievers resemble grave-dwellers who neither benefit from nor accept what they hear.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:19-22/r18.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعيسى الثقفي وعمرو بن ميمون: «بمسمع من في القبور» بحذف التنوين تخفيفا

RAZI-FULL:v26p15/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p15/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p15/r1.claim: After contrasting guidance and misguidance, al-Razi identifies the believer as seeing the clear path and the unbeliever as blind.
RAZI-FULL:v26p15/r1.anchor: لما بين الهدى والضلالة ولم يهتد الكافر ، وهدى الله المؤمن من ضرب لهم مثلا بالبصير والأعمى

RAZI-FULL:v26p15/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p15/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p15/r2.claim: The blind and seeing represent believer and unbeliever; darkness and light represent unbelief and faith, with the unbeliever burdened by blindness as well as darkness.
RAZI-FULL:v26p15/r2.anchor: وقال الإيمان نور والمؤمن بصير والبصير لا يخفى عليه النور ، والكفر ظلمة والكافر أعمى فله صاد فوق صاد

RAZI-FULL:v26p15/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p15/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p15/r4.claim: The living and dead are another comparison: a blind person shares some perception with the seeing, but an unbeliever has no beneficial perception and is like the dead; the repeated verb sets this image apart.
RAZI-FULL:v26p15/r4.anchor: فإن الأعمى يشارك البصير في إدراك ما . والكافر غير مدرك إدراكا نافعا فهو كالميت

RAZI-FULL:v26p15/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p15/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p15/r5.claim: Negation repeats where the contrasts are strongest: darkness and light, and shade and heat, are direct opposites; life and death differ more essentially than seeing and blindness, so the final contrast also merits emphasis.
RAZI-FULL:v26p15/r5.anchor: التكرير للتأكيد والمنافاة بين الظلمة والنور والظل والحرور مضادة ، فالظلمة تنافي النور وتضاده والعمى والبصر كذلك

RAZI-FULL:v26p16/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p16/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p16/r4.claim: The living are believers who accepted God's revelation; the dead are those who heard clear verses but gained no benefit, and are placed after the believers because their spiritual death followed the believers' life.
RAZI-FULL:v26p16/r4.anchor: أي المؤمنون الذين آمنوا بما أنزل الله والأموات الذين تليت عليهم الآيات البينات

RAZI-FULL:v26p16#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p16#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p16#2/r2.claim: Living and dead are plural because the gap is absolute: no dead person equals any living person in perception, whether kinds or individuals are compared.
RAZI-FULL:v26p16#2/r2.anchor: ما من ميت يساوي في الإدراك حيا من الأحياء

RAZI-FULL:v26p17/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p17/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p17/r1.claim: One possible reading contrasts divine and prophetic hearing: God can make the dead hear, while the Prophet cannot make buried people hear; the disbelievers likewise cannot hear his recitation and revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v26p17/r1.anchor: أن يكون المراد بيان كون الكفار بالنسبة إلى سماعهم كلام النبي والوحي النازل عليه دون حال الموتى فإن الله يسمع الموتى

RAZI-FULL:v26p17/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p17/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p17/r2.claim: Alternatively, the verse consoles Muhammad: only God can make them hear, even if they were deaf rocks, so he bears no responsibility for their response.
RAZI-FULL:v26p17/r2.anchor: وأما أنت فلا تسمع من في القبور

STUDYQURAN:35:22/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:22/r1.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:35:22/r1.claim: Ṭ identifies the living as people whose hearts are alive with faith and the dead as people whose hearts are dead under disbelief; this answers questions in 6:122 and 39:22.
STUDYQURAN:35:22/r1.anchor: those who hear the truth of the revelation, while those whose hearts are buried in the grave of ignorance cannot hear it (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:35:22/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:22/r2.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:35:22/r2.claim: Aj explains God’s causing people to hear as His guiding and supporting them.
STUDYQURAN:35:22/r2.anchor: God’s causing them to hear thus refers to His guiding them and supporting them (Aj)

QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r6.claim: Blind and seeing, darkness and light, shade and heat, and living and dead are unlike states and cannot be equated.
QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r6.anchor: كما لا يستوي الأعمى والبصير لا تستوي الظلمات والنور

QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r7.claim: The contrasts signify those joined to God versus distracted from Him, drawn near versus veiled, chosen versus forsaken, and made witnesses versus heedless.
QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r7.anchor: وكذلك لا يستوي الموصول بنا والمشغول عنا ، والمجذوب إلينا

QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r8.speaker: منشدون
QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r8.claim: An anonymous poem says God's lovers differ sharply from those who oppose Him.

TAB-FULL:v19p357/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p357/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p357/r1.claim: Living hearts believe in God and His Messenger and know revelation; dead hearts overwhelmed by disbelief cannot understand God's commands or distinguish guidance from error. The contrasts portray belief and disbelief.
TAB-FULL:v19p357/r1.anchor: والإيمان، والكافر والكفر وبنحو الذي قلنا في ذلك قال أهل التأويل

TAB-FULL:v19p357/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p357/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p357/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says blindness, darkness, heat, and death portray disobedience; sight, light, shade, and life portray obedience.
TAB-FULL:v19p357/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وما يستوي الأعمى والبصير} [فاطر: 19] الآية، قال: " هو مثل ضربه الله لأهل الطاعة وأهل المعصية

TAB-FULL:v19p357/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p357/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p357/r3.claim: Qatada describes believers as alive in effect, sight, intention, and action, while disbelievers are dead in sight, heart, and action.
TAB-FULL:v19p357/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وما يستوي الأعمى} [فاطر: 19] «الآية خلقا، فضل بعضه على بعض؛ فأما المؤمن فعبد حي الأثر، حي البصر

TAB-FULL:v19p357/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p357/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v19p357/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says the believer sees his religion while the disbeliever is blind; the living person given light represents guidance into Islam, unlike the blind heart in darkness.
TAB-FULL:v19p357/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {وما يستوي الأعمى والبصير ولا الظلمات ولا النور ولا الظل ولا الحرور وما يستوي الأحياء ولا الأموات}

TAB-FULL:v19p359/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p359/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p359/r1.claim: As the dead in graves cannot hear scripture and be guided, the Prophet cannot make spiritually dead people benefit from admonition, proofs, or revelation.
TAB-FULL:v19p359/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {إن الله يسمع من يشاء وما أنت بمسمع من في القبور} [فاطر: 22] «كذلك الكافر لا يسمع، ولا ينتفع بما يسمع»

TAB-FULL:v19p359/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p359/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p359/r2.claim: Qatada says the disbeliever neither hears nor benefits from what he hears.
TAB-FULL:v19p359/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {إن الله يسمع من يشاء وما أنت بمسمع من في القبور} [فاطر: 22] «كذلك الكافر لا يسمع، ولا ينتفع بما يسمع»

TABATABAI:35:18-22/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:18-22/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:18-22/r6.claim: Repeating the negating particle through these successive comparisons reinforces the denial of equality.
TABATABAI:35:18-22/r6.anchor: تكرار حروف النفي مرة بعد مرة في الآية وما يليها لتأكيد النفي

TABATABAI:35:18-22/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:18-22/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:18-22/r10.claim: The living/dead comparison continues the blind/sighted comparison. Repeating the formula after the long interruption keeps its meaning present, as in the repeated questions in 9:7–8.
TABATABAI:35:18-22/r10.anchor: { ما يستوي } لئلا يغيب المعنى عن ذهن السامع فهو كقوله

TABATABAI:35:18-22/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:18-22/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:18-22/r11.claim: The successive likenesses represent believers and disbelievers and the consequences of their deeds.
TABATABAI:35:18-22/r11.anchor: الجمل المتوالية المترتبة أعني قوله { وما يستوي الأعمى والبصير } إلى قوله

TABATABAI:35:18-22/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:18-22/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:18-22/r12.claim: God enables the believer to hear: spiritually dead before, the believer is revived and made receptive because of an inner readiness for it.
TABATABAI:35:18-22/r12.anchor: وهو المؤمن كان ميتا فأحياه الله فأسمعه لما في نفسه من الاستعداد لذلك

TABATABAI:35:22-26/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:22-26/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:22-26/r1.claim: The Prophet is only an instrument; guidance itself comes from God.
TABATABAI:35:22-26/r1.anchor: وأما النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فإنما هو وسيلة والهدى هدى الله

TABATABAI:35:22-26/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:22-26/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:22-26/r2.claim: Those described as being in graves are the disbelievers whose hearts have been sealed.
TABATABAI:35:22-26/r2.anchor: أي الأموات والمراد بهم الكفار المطبوع على قلوبهم

TABRISI:35:18-22/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:18-22/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:18-22/r3.claim: To make someone hear is to bring about an audible sound in a form the hearer can perceive.
TABRISI:35:18-22/r3.anchor: والاسماع إيجاد المسموع بحيث يدركه السامع

TABRISI:35:18-22/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:18-22/r21.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:18-22/r21.claim: The living and dead represent believers and unbelievers.
TABRISI:35:18-22/r21.anchor: يعني المؤمنين والكافرين. وقيل: يعني العلماء

TABRISI:35:18-22/r22.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:18-22/r22.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:35:18-22/r22.claim: Another interpretation is scholars and ignorant people.
TABRISI:35:18-22/r22.anchor: وقيل: يعني العلماء والجهال وقال بعضهم

TABRISI:35:18-22/r24.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:18-22/r24.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:18-22/r24.claim: God benefits through hearing whomever He wills to favor and guide; this does not deny that unbelievers literally heard His signs.
TABRISI:35:18-22/r24.anchor: أي ينفع بالإسماع من يشاء أن يلطف له ويوفقه ولم يرد به نفي حقيقة السماع

TABRISI:35:18-22/r25.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:18-22/r25.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:18-22/r25.claim: The Prophet cannot make unbelievers benefit from hearing when they refuse to accept, just as the dead in graves cannot hear.
TABRISI:35:18-22/r25.anchor: أي إنك لا تقدر على أن تنفع الكفار بإسماعك إياهم إذ لم يقبلوا

THALABI:v8p104#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p104#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p104#2/r6.claim: The living are believers and the dead are unbelievers; God enables whom He wills to hear, take admonition, and respond, while the Prophet cannot make unbelievers hear, for they are like the dead.
THALABI:v8p104#2/r6.anchor: وما يستوي الأحياء ولا الأموات يعني: المؤمنين والكفار. إن الله يسمع من يشاء، حتى يتعظ ويجيب وما أنت بمسمع من في القبور يعني: الكفار شبههم بالأموات،

THALABI:v8p104#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p104#2/r7.speaker: أشهب العقيلي
THALABI:v8p104#2/r7.claim: Ashhab al-Uqayli reads بمسمع without nunation, construing it in an annexation.
THALABI:v8p104#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ أشهب العقيلي: (بمسمع من في القبور) بلا تنوين على الإضافة.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p361#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p361#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p361#4/r1.claim: The living and the dead are a comparison for intelligent and ignorant people.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p361#4/r1.anchor: وما يستوي الأحياء ولا الأموات} مثل للعقلاء والجهال.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r1.claim: The living are believers and the dead are disbelievers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says a disbeliever is like a dead person despite eating, drinking, coming, and going; he cites “dead, not living” (16:21).
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الكافر وإن كان يأكل ويشرب ويجيء ويذهب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God enables His allies—those created for Paradise and protected from disbelief—to hear.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يسمع أولياءه (¬1) الذين خلقهم لجنته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r4.claim: God lets whomever He wills hear His words so that they take heed and find guidance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r4.anchor: والمعنى: يسمع كلامه من يشاء حتى يتعظ يهتدي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r5.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r5.claim: Al-Suddī explains “He makes hear” as “He guides whom He wills.”

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r6.claim: Those in graves represent disbelievers: they are like the dead because they are deaf to and do not answer the call to faith.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r6.anchor: يعني: الكفار، شبههم حين صموا ولم يجيبوا إذا دعوا إلى الإيمان بأهل القبور

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r8.claim: The living are believers and the dead are unbelievers; God enables whom He wills to hear and benefit.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r8.anchor: يعني: المؤمنين والكفار { إن الله يسمع من يشاء } فينتفع بذلك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r9.claim: The people in graves are unbelievers compared to the dead: just as grave-dwellers do not hear, unbelievers do not hear the message.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r9.anchor: يعني: الكفار، شبههم بالأموات، أي: كما لا يسمع أصحاب القبور كذلك لا يسمع الكفار

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784#2/r1.claim: The contrasts of seas, sight, darkness and light, shade and heat, and life and death all picture the difference between believer and unbeliever.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784#2/r1.anchor: هذا كله مثل للمؤمن والكافر، كما لا يستوي البحران العذب والمالح، وكما لا يستوي الأعمى والبصير

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784#2/r2.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says the dead are the unbelievers, who are like the dead, and the living are the believers.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784#2/r2.anchor: وقال السدي: وهذا مثل ضربه الله للكفار والمؤمنين، فالأموات هم الكفار

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784#2/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784#2/r4.claim: Believers are alive in religion, as in 6:122, where God gives life through faith.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784#2/r4.anchor: قال: {وما يستوي الأحياء} [فاطر: 22] المؤمنون الأحياء في الدين كقوله: {أومن كان ميتا فأحييناه}

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p785/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p785/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p785/r1.claim: The dead are the unbelievers in religion.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p785/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p785/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p785/r2.claim: God makes those whom He wills hear by guiding them to faith.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p785/r2.anchor: {إن الله يسمع من يشاء} [فاطر: 22] يهديه للإيمان.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p785/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p785/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p785/r3.claim: The Prophet cannot make unbelievers accept guidance; they are like the dead, who do not hear those in this world.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p785/r3.anchor: {وما أنت بمسمع من في القبور} [فاطر: 22] ، أي: وما أنت بمسمع الكفار

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r1.speaker: Müfessirlerin genel kanaati
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r1.claim: Commentators generally take the positive comparisons to represent truth, faith, believers, and their good reward, and the negative ones to represent falsehood, unbelief, disbelievers, and their bad end.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r1.anchor: Müfessirlerin genel kanaatine göre bu karşılaştırmalı örneklerin olumlu olanları hakkı, imanı, iman sahiplerini ve kavuşacakları güzellikleri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r2.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r2.claim: The believer's path, insight, resolve, and lasting useful deeds contrast with the disbeliever's lifelessness, blindness, darkened heart, and futile works.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r2.anchor: Müminin tuttuğu yol sağlam, ufku ve basireti açık, niyet ve iradesi güçlü, yaptıkları kalıcı ve yarayışlıdır; kâfir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r3.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r3.claim: Razi maps sight to believers, blindness to disbelievers, light to faith, darkness to unbelief, shade to comfort, heat to hardship and fire, and life and death to believers and disbelievers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r3.anchor: Râzî bu örneklere şöyle bir izah getirir (XXVI, 16): “Gören” kelimesi mümini, “kör” kelimesi kâfiri, “aydınlık” imanı, “karanlıklar” küfrü

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r4.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r4.claim: The believer sees the clear path to a new life after this world, while the unbeliever cannot see it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r4.anchor: Zira mümin önündeki açık yolu (dünya hayatından sonra yeni bir hayatın başlayacağını) görmekte, inkârcı ise bunu görmemektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r5.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r5.claim: Even sound eyesight cannot see without light: faith illuminates the path, whereas unbelief is darkness that blocks the truth.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r5.anchor: İşte iman ışık demektir ki gören kişinin önünü aydınlatır, küfür ise karanlığı temsil ettiğinden kâfirin hakikati görmesine engeldir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r6.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r6.claim: The images also point to outcomes: believers find ease and peace, while disbelievers face hardship and scorching fire.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r6.anchor: müminin rahata ve huzura kavuşacağına, kâfirin ise sıkıntı ve yakıcı ateş ile karşılaşacağına işaret edilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r7.claim: A comparison of sighted and blind people understates the believer-disbeliever divide: a blind person still grasps some things, but an unbeliever has no useful perception and is like the dead.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r7.anchor: Mümin ve kâfirin durumunu anlatmaya, gören ile körün mukayesesi bile az gelir. Çünkü âmâ bazı şeyleri idrak etmede gören ile ortak özelliğe sahiptir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r8.claim: The repeated ‘are not equal’ verb at verse 22, in the contrast between the living and dead, supports this interpretation of verse 19.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r8.anchor: 19. âyette geçen “bir olmaz” fiilinin dirilerle ölülerden söz eden 22. âyette tekrar edilmesi de bu yorumu desteklemektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r9.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r9.claim: Razi says repeating the negation emphasizes the later comparisons: the first pair is not opposites to the same degree, while the other pairs are opposites in their nature.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r9.anchor: Râzî, gören ile kör mukayesesinde olumsuzluk edatının tekrar edilmeyip diğerlerinde tekrar edilmesinde şöyle bir mâna inceliği bulunduğunu belirtir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r10.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r10.claim: Razi adds that sight and blindness can apply to one person and the blind share some cognition with the sighted, whereas living and dead differ in reality and have no such common ground.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r10.anchor: ölü sadece vasıf açısından değil işin gerçeği ve mahiyeti bakımından da diriden farklıdır (XXVI, 16; bu konuda başka görüşler için bk. Taberî

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r11.speaker: Bazı müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r11.claim: Some exegetes take the living and dead as learned and ignorant people; others take them as those who reason and those who do not.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r11.anchor: Bazı müfessirlere göre ise diriler ve ölüler örneği, âlimlerle câhilleri, bazılarına göre de aklını kullananlarla aklını kullanmayanları anlatmaktadır (Şevkânî

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r12.speaker: İbn Atıyye
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r12.claim: The final clause compares those who ignore all proofs and persist stubbornly in disbelief to the dead in their graves.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r12.anchor: 22. âyetin son cümlesinde, getirilen bütün kanıtları görmezden gelen ve inatla inkârcılığını sürdürenler kabirlerdekilere yani ölülere benzetilmiştir (İbn Atıyye

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r13.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r13.claim: Razi offers two purposes for the comparison: the disbelievers have completely stopped their ears to the Prophet's message, or nothing he does can awaken their understanding.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:19/r13.anchor: bu benzetmedeki maksat, inkârcıların Resûlullah’ın bildirdiklerine kulaklarını tamamen tıkamış olduklarını belirtmek olabileceği gibi, o ne yaparsa yapsın onların iz‘anını harekete geçiremeyeceğini

ITQAN:v3p182#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p182#2/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p182#2/r7.claim: The Qur'an also repeats examples, including contrasts between blind and seeing, darkness and light, shade and heat, and living and dead.

NAHHAS:v3p369/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p369/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v3p369/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies living and dead as believers and unbelievers, darkness and light as error and guidance, and shade and heat as paradise and fire.
NAHHAS:v3p369/r1.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس قال المؤمن والكافر قال و ( الظلمات ) الضلالة و ( النور ) الهدى

NAHHAS:v3p369/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p369/r2.speaker: الأخفش سعيد
NAHHAS:v3p369/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash says لا is extra, so darkness and light, shade and heat are simply not equal.
NAHHAS:v3p369/r2.anchor: قال الأخفش سعيد لا زائدة والمعنى ولا الظلمات والنور ولا الظل والحرور

NAHHAS:v3p369/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p369/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p369/r3.claim: One view restricts حرور to night and سموم to day; the preferred view allows حرور at either time because its intensive form denotes harmful heat.
NAHHAS:v3p369/r3.anchor: وقيل الحرور لا يكون إلا بالليل والسموم يكون بالنهار وقيل الحرور يكون فيهما وهذا أصح القولين

NAHHAS:v3p369/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p369/r4.speaker: الحسن
NAHHAS:v3p369/r4.claim: Al-Hasan reads without tanwin on مسمع for ease; the dead are like those who do not benefit from or accept what they hear.
NAHHAS:v3p369/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( وما أنت بمسمع من في القبور ) تحذف التنوين تخفيفا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r4.claim: A third sense is guidance: the guided person is described as alive.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r4.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الحياة في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

TABATABAI:35:15-26/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:15-26/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:15-26/r1.claim: The quoted wording does not match the Qur'anic text: its opening comes from 27:80 and its ending from 35:22.
TABATABAI:35:15-26/r1.anchor: على أن ما نقله من الآية لا يطابق المصحف فصدره مأخوذ من سورة النمل الآية 80 وذيله مأخوذ من سورة فاطر الآية 22

TABATABAI:35:15-26/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:15-26/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:15-26/r2.claim: The verse occurs in a Meccan context, surrounded by other Meccan verses.
TABATABAI:35:15-26/r2.anchor: على أن سياق الآية مكي في سياق آيات سابقة ولاحقة مكية

BURHAN:v3p23/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p23/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p23/r6.claim: He cites the repeated contrasts between blind and seeing, darkness and light, shade and heat, and living and dead as repetition of comparisons.

ITQAN:v3p34/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p34/r10.speaker: ابن الصائغ
ITQAN:v3p34/r10.claim: The third purpose is honor: examples put men before women, the free before the enslaved, the living before the dead, and hearing before sight. Ibn ʿAtiyya reports al-Naqqash’s argument that this ordering favors hearing and sight.
ITQAN:v3p34/r10.anchor: الثالث التشريف كتقديم الذكر على الأنثى نحو

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p290/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p290/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p290/r6.claim: Because mercy and punishment belong to God, the following passage challenges idolaters to prove their deities' partnership; if their claim rests only on arrogance, the Prophet should leave their case to God, the best judge.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p290/r6.anchor: It is evident from the previous verses that mercy and punishment are in the hands of God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r6.claim: Section III (verses 19-28) moves to the kinds of people who accept faith and those deprived of it, using contrasts in nature to illuminate this difference.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r6.anchor: The succeeding verses state the types of people who will accept faith and the types who will be deprived from it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r7.claim: Light and darkness, heat and cold, and fertile land flourishing in rain versus barren land despite abundant rain illustrate different human tendencies.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r7.anchor: there are fertile lands which become lush green because of rain and there also barren lands which in spite of abundant rain do not bear any produce.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r8.claim: The Qur'an is like rain: vibrant, living hearts benefit from it, while those dead in heart and mind are deprived of its blessing.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r8.anchor: which is pouring down on them in the form of the Qur’ān

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r9.claim: God created natural opposites for the universe's benefit and gives respite to people inclined to vice as well as those inclined to virtue.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r9.anchor: for the overall benefit of the universe in a similar manner He has given respite to people who like vice

JISHUMI:v8p5839/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5839/r1.speaker: قراءة العامة
JISHUMI:v8p5839/r1.claim: The general reading has bi-mismaʿ with genitive and nunation, while min is accusative in position.
JISHUMI:v8p5839/r1.anchor: قراءة العامة: (بمسمع) بالجر والتنوين، (من في القبور) (من) محله نصب

JISHUMI:v8p5839/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5839/r2.speaker: أشهب العقيلي
JISHUMI:v8p5839/r2.claim: Ashhab reads bi-mismaʿ without nunation in an annexation construction, making min genitive.
JISHUMI:v8p5839/r2.anchor: وقرأ أشهب العقيلي بلا تنوين على الإضافة، و(من) محله جر

JISHUMI:v8p5839/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5839/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5839/r9.claim: Samʿ is perceiving what is heard and also means the ear, the organ by which hearing occurs.
JISHUMI:v8p5839/r9.anchor: والسمع: مصدر سمع سمعا، وهو إدراك المسموع، والسمع: الأذن؛ لأنه يسمع به

JISHUMI:v8p5839/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5839/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5839/r10.claim: Ismāʿ is making a sound heard so that it can be perceived.
JISHUMI:v8p5839/r10.anchor: والإسماع: إيجاب المسموع بحيث يدركه، أسمع يسمع إسماعا فهو مسمع
